metadata.name: net-displacement-power-phase5
metadata.intent: Paper-grade power comparison of the net-displacement orientation estimator against PC1 at the Phase 5 design (n = 1200, four stages, group_ratio 0.5, all three blocks, joint magnitude): pls_cv x net_displacement vs pls_cv x pc1 on matched datasets over magnitude, orientation, shape and translation at 500 replicates x 999 permutations, judged by the predeclared column decision rule with a no-loss criterion on orientation/angle (roadmap Next changes item 2).
metadata.motivating_evidence: docs/reports/orientation-measurement-probe-2026-10-12.md (Phase 5 orientation/angle PC1 0.84-0.88, net_displacement 0.89-0.93; shape -> angle leak 0.89 -> 0.02); docs/reports/net-displacement-type-i-2026-10-13.md (lead-arm anchor angle 0.050)
notes: Design grid, explicit form, two measurement columns on matched datasets over evaluation.integration_method x evaluation.orientation_estimator: pls_cv x pc1 (baseline, served by the primary power grid) and pls_cv x net_displacement (the candidate). No concat, pca, forced-rank or pls_within_group column (change net-displacement-power-comparison, proposal and design D3): the concat ceiling is cited from the orientation measurement probe and the Type I study.

The two columns share everything but angle: the estimator enters estimate_difference only through the orientation statistic and evaluation.seed = 3 is also the RRPP seed, so delta and shape p-values and observed statistics are identical record for record between the columns. scripts/net_displacement_power_checks.py verifies this and the baseline column's reproduction of the parent records.

acceptance.column_decision is the predeclared, advisory rule (design D1/D2): candidate pls_cv x net_displacement against the baseline column at each mode's top effect; target orientation/angle; anchor and the mandatory controls translation/angle, magnitude/angle and shape/angle held to 0.05 + 2 * sqrt(0.05 * 0.95 / R) (0.0695 at R = 500); protected magnitude/delta and shape/shape (identical between the two pls_cv columns, so they pass with loss 0 by construction). scripts/net_displacement_power_follow_up.py reads both profiles' column_decision.json.

Every Type I and specificity acceptance target uses bound 'upper'. The Phase 4 gate and attribution are off and acceptance.power is empty: the column rule is the predeclared decision here. No report_contract: do not pass --n-jobs.
surgery_censoring stays at its default ('error'); every pool-limited cell is under headroom at e = 1.0 (the parent profiles enumerate the same cells), so enumeration rejects nothing.
Cells: 2 Type I baselines + 2 columns x (1 anchor + 4 modes x 4 effects) = 36 cells, 18,000 work units.

generator (other than magnitude_kind), evaluation, base_seed 600 and the matched-seed family phase5-primary are copied verbatim from phase5_power_study.json; magnitude_kind is 'joint' (the production construction). Orientation, shape, translation and the zero-effect anchor ignore magnitude_kind, so the baseline column re-evaluates results/phase5-2026-09-10's datasets with its permutation draws at 0.25-1.0; magnitude at 0.25 and 1.0 reproduces results/phase5-magnitude-2026-10-08.

Magnitude at e = 0.5 and 0.75 are new cells under the joint construction (no Phase 5 parent record). One effect_sizes list serves all four modes (design D3); the comparison reads only the magnitude/angle leak.

criterion 'no_loss' (design D1): PC1 already saturates orientation/angle at Phase 5 (0.84-0.88 in the probe), so requiring a 2-pooled-SE gain would fail the candidate for not improving a test at its ceiling; the candidate must not fall below the baseline by more than 2 pooled MC SEs.

Planning figure: about 74 s per pls_cv unit at 999 permutations (Type I run, under contention) -> about 370 core-hours, the largest single study so far. Go/no-go (design Risks): if the timing job's projection with a 20 % margin exceeds 450 core-hours, drop e = 0.75 (28 cells, about 290 core-hours), re-pin this profile's identity entry and say so here and in the report.

submission.nodes: check sinfo -N -o '%N %T %C %e' first and exclude nodes under memory pressure or NFS stalls
submission.budget: ~370 core-hours planning figure; > 450 projected with 20 % margin -> drop e = 0.75
